M_note: Measured after execution and deduplication; never a promised number.

environments.task: Reverse an English sentence character by character and put the result in <reversed_text> tags. Data comes from HF PrimeIntellect/Reverse-Text-RL (train). The system prompt asks for the tags, and the gold answer is prompt[::-1].
environments.reward: One reward, lcs_reward_func, weight 1.0. It takes vf.XMLParser(['reversed_text']).parse_answer(completion), or '' if nothing parses, and returns difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, parsed, answer).ratio(). The env wraps it in a RubricGroup that adds a num_turns metric, which does not change the reward. Full credit (1.0) means the content of the first <reversed_text>...</reversed_text> in the last assistant message equals answer exactly after the parser strips whitespace.

environments.task: Turn an English description of a directory hierarchy into an ASCII tree (' +--', ' `--', ' |   ' style) inside <ascii_formatted> tags. Data comes from HF kalomaze/ascii-tree-mix-it1 (train), with gold = verification_info.ground_truth.
environments.reward: Two rewards, weighted 0.3 and 0.7. ascii_tree_similarity_reward (0.3) is difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio over the lists of lines of parsed vs gold. ascii_tree_continuous_reward (0.7) is the longest matching block of lines divided by the number of gold lines. Each reward is halved if a non-first line does not start with ' ' (and is not equal to the first line), and halved again if no non-first line contains '--'. The parser is XMLParser(['think','ascii_formatted']) with answer_field ascii_formatted, and a RubricGroup adds a num_turns metric. Full credit is 1.0.

environments.task: MATH-500 competition math (HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500 test split, pinned revision). The prompt is the problem plus 'Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.' The model must box the final answer.
environments.reward: One reward: Math500Task.correct, weight 1.0 = vf.verify_boxed_math_answer(trace.last_reply, data.answer) from verifiers/v1/utils/score.py. It returns 0 if the reply contains '<think>' without '</think>'. Otherwise it takes the text after the last '</think>', extracts the content of the LAST \boxed{...} (strict, brace-balanced, '' if there is no box), extracts the gold the same way (falling back to the raw gold), and runs math_verify parse('\boxed{gold}') vs parse('\boxed{pred}') with verify() and 5s timeouts. Any exception scores 0. Binary, so full credit is 1.0.
